title: Assemble every VCF Automation catalog item page in stable order
prompt:
Implement `src/VcfCatalogClient.java` as a single-file, JDK-only client for the Catalog service of VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. Add no dependencies and edit no other file; the supplied `src/Json.java` reads and writes JSON for you.

VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation and publishes no OpenAPI document: it is absent from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, and no machine-readable specification for the Catalog service is offered on the Broadcom Developer Portal. The protected `docs/contract.json` was therefore transcribed by hand from the rendered xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com, and it states in its own `source_statement` that its source is reference documentation rather than a published specification. `docs/official_sources.json` records every page URL, the operation each documents, and the date it was fetched. Where the documentation is silent, `docs/contract.json` records an explicit choice under `local_decisions`. Treat that file as authoritative and read it before you write code.

The contract admits exactly one operation, `getCatalogItems`, which is `GET /catalog/api/items`. Call no other route. The administrative route `GET /catalog/api/admin/items` and the per-item route `GET /catalog/api/items/{id}` are documented in the sources but deliberately excluded, so the whole collection must be assembled from the paginated route alone.

Keep the supplied public API exactly as declared:

- `VcfCatalogClient(String baseUrl, String accessToken)`
- `VcfCatalogClient(String baseUrl, String accessToken, Duration timeout)`
- `VcfCatalogClient.VcfAutomationException`, thrown for invalid input, transport or HTTP failure, and malformed or inconsistent responses
- `List<String> listCatalogItems(int pageSize, String search, List<String> projectIds)`

`listCatalogItems` must retrieve the collection completely. Request `page=0` first and advance by exactly one page until every element has been collected, buffering everything and throwing rather than returning a partial collection if the walk cannot finish. Reject a `pageSize` below 1 before any request leaves the client. Require each response to be a `PageCatalogItem` object carrying a `content` array and the integral members `number`, `size`, `totalElements` and `totalPages`; reject a response whose `number` is not the page requested, whose `size` is not the page size requested, whose totals change part-way through the walk, whose page is overfull, or which otherwise fails to make progress. Require every element to be an object whose contract-required `id` and `name` are nonblank strings, with case-sensitively unique ids. Reject a null, blank or non-absolute `baseUrl`, a null or blank `accessToken`, and a null or non-positive `timeout`. Never place the access token in an exception message.

Return one line per catalog item formatted as `name + "\t" + id + "\t" + typeId`, where `typeId` is the `id` member of the item's `type` object. Every member of a `ResourceReference` is documented as optional, so emit the single character `-` when `type` carries no usable id. Sort the completed collection by `name` and then by `id`, both ascending and case-sensitive. Local ordering is required rather than optional: the server's `sort=name,asc` does not fix the relative order of equal names, so page order alone is unstable.

Honor the exact wire contract. Every request is a bodyless GET carrying exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` header and exactly one `Accept: application/json` header, and no `Content-Type` or `Content-Length`. Send `page` and `size` explicitly on every request rather than relying on documented defaults, and send `sort` exactly once with the value `name,asc`. Emit parameters in the contract order `page`, `size`, `sort`, `search`, `projects`, percent-encoded as UTF-8, so that the comma in the sort value travels as `sort=name%2Casc` and a reserved character in a caller-supplied value cannot be read as a delimiter. Repeat `projects` once per project id, in caller order, on every page. Omit every unset optional parameter entirely: `search` and `projects` when the caller supplies none, and `types`, `expandProjects`, `expand`, `$top`, `$skip` and `$orderby` always. Omitted means the parameter name does not appear at all, never a blank value, a zero, a false, or a bare delimiter.

Run `bash .protected/verify.sh`. It compiles the harness together with your client and runs `TestMain`, which builds catalog fixtures and a bearer token at runtime, starts a mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port whose route table is derived from the operations named in `docs/contract.json`, drives your client, and then reads the mock's flushed JSONL request log. Verification asserts the complete stably ordered output, the request count, the exact raw request target of every page, header multiplicity, empty bodies, and the omission of every unset optional parameter. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint.

source_basis.reason: VCF Automation has no OpenAPI document in https://github.com/vmware/vcf-api-specs and no downloadable specification for the Catalog service on the Broadcom Developer Portal, so the contract was derived from rendered reference pages instead.
source_basis.api_title_as_published: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Catalog
source_basis.operation_id_provenance: Contract-local. The reference pages render the human title 'Get Catalog Items' and the summary 'Fetch a list of catalog items'; no machine operationId is published.

scenario: Forty-seven catalog items, including duplicate names and a case-differing pair, arrive across several getCatalogItems pages with equal names ordered unstably, and must be collected completely before stable projection and sorting.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact bodyless GET wire shape, the percent-encoded sort value, the repeated projects parameter, and the omission of every unset optional query parameter.
